concepts.title: Concept of Business: Economic Activity with Profit Motive
concepts.definition: Business is an economic activity involving the production or purchase and sale of goods and services with the objective of earning profit by satisfying human needs in society.
concepts.key_idea: Business undertakings deal in goods and services on a regular basis, bear risk and uncertainty, and reward the entrepreneur with profit for bearing it.
question_patterns: define business as an economic activity
state the characteristics of business
why is business regarded as an economic activity
explain the profit motive of business
how does business deal with risk and uncertainty
distinguish business from employment and profession

solution_steps.explain: Check sale or exchange of goods and services, regularity, profit motive and risk.
Separate wage work and professional practice from business undertaking.
Confirm the activity satisfies human needs in society.

concepts.title: Industry and Its Types: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary
concepts.definition: Industry refers to economic activities that convert resources into useful goods, grouped as primary industries extracting nature's products, secondary industries manufacturing and construction, and tertiary industries providing support services.
concepts.key_idea: Genetic industries like poultry and mining extractive work sit beside manufacturing industries that process materials into finished goods.
question_patterns: classify industries into primary secondary and tertiary
what are genetic industries with examples
how does manufacturing differ from construction industry
define extractive industries with examples
give the classification of industry on the basis of size and ownership
which industries provide support services to business

solution_steps.explain: See whether the activity extracts, processes or supports.
Place the industry in primary, secondary or tertiary group.
Match with mining, textiles or banking style examples.

concepts.title: Commerce: Trade and Aids to Trade
concepts.definition: Commerce includes all activities that remove the hindrances of person, place, time, risk, finance and knowledge between producers and consumers, and it has two branches, namely trade and aids to trade.
concepts.key_idea: Trade is the buying and selling of goods, while banking, insurance, transport, warehousing, advertising and communication act as aids to trade.
question_patterns: define commerce and name its two branches
how do aids to trade remove hindrances of business
distinguish between internal trade and external trade
what is the role of warehousing and insurance in commerce
explain the hindrance of place and its remedy
how does advertising remove the hindrance of knowledge

solution_steps.explain: Note the obstacle between producer and consumer.
Pair transport for place, insurance for risk, banking for finance.
Separate buying and selling from supporting services.

concepts.title: Business Risk: Nature and Causes
concepts.definition: Business risk refers to the possibility of inadequate profits or losses because of uncertainties or unexpected events, and it arises from natural, human, economic and other causes.
concepts.key_idea: Risk is an essential part of business, its degree depends on the scale of operations, and profit is the reward for taking risk.
question_patterns: define business risk and state its nature
what are the causes of business risk
why is profit called the reward of risk taking
how does the scale of operations affect business risk
distinguish insurable and non insurable risks
explain natural and human causes of business risk

solution_steps.explain: Identify the unexpected event behind the possible loss.
Place the cause as natural, human, economic or physical.
State how risk bearing earns the reward of profit.
